1.title: Two Classic Mirabelle Varieties
1.html:
Strictly speaking, Mirabelle is a specialty of neighbouring Lorraine, but because Alsace and Lorraine are geographically adjacent and their food cultures closely intertwined, Mirabelle de Lorraine is also an indispensable spirit companion at the Alsace table. Two main varieties are grown locally:

  • Mirabelle de Metz: fine skin, yellow with red spots, ripening in August
  • Mirabelle de Nancy: larger than the Metz variety, with an evenly yellow skin, ripening in mid-August

Both are protected by a geographical indication (IGP), certified together under the name "Mirabelle de Lorraine".

A mirabelle tree must be planted for a full eight years before it starts to bear fruit, and a mature tree can yield up to 100 kg of mirabelles a year (about 10,000 fruits) — these orchards, covering about 2,000 ha, form an important pillar of the agricultural economy of Lorraine.
3.title: Rigorous Appellation and Distillation Rules
3.html:
The Eau-de-vie (spirit) appellation for Mirabelle de Lorraine was already regulated on 30 November 1953, covering the four départements of Meurthe-et-Moselle, Moselle, Meuse and Vosges.

  • Fermentation rules: fermentation of the fruit must take place naturally, without heating or adding any chemicals, and the fermentation period must be at least 15 days
  • Still: a pot still (à repasse) may be used, or single-run (premier jet discontinu) equipment heated by open flame / steam
  • Strength at distillation: no more than 70% vol.
  • Strength at sale: at least 45% vol.
  • Non-alcohol substance content: less than 400 g per hundred litres of pure alcohol (g/hl pure alcohol), of which esters must be at least 200 g — the key to the fruity ester character typical of Mirabelle brandy
4.question: What strict rule applies to the fermentation of Mirabelle de Lorraine spirit?
4.options.0: Yeast may be added freely to speed fermentation
4.options.1: Fermentation must be natural, without heating or adding any chemicals, and must last at least 15 days
4.options.2: There is no limit on fermentation time; the faster the better
4.options.3: Commercial yeast strains must be used
4.explanation: The Mirabelle de Lorraine regulation expressly states that fermentation of the fruit must be natural, without heating or adding any chemicals, and must last at least 15 days — a rule ensuring the spirit truly reflects the mirabelle's own natural flavour, and at the core of the quality guarantee of this traditional fruit spirit.
